rootCause: Malformed new test harness identifier, not a production defect. shard4_harness.vs2_t equals fixtures_r1.c2_hash byte for byte (28 bytes of 0xc2), so shard4.identities_distinct always returns False on every honest transaction. Every failing path conjoins that predicate; every passing split, financial and piece bench avoids it.
exactEvidence: shard4_harness.ak:25-26 (parent M): pub const vs2_t = #"c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2c2" (identical string)
shard4.ak identities_distinct: ids = [c2_hash, vi_hash, policy, ..pieces]; requires 4 pieces, every id 28 bytes, and list.unique length equality, so the duplicated 0xc2 value alone forces False

OPX2-compare.json statusNotPass lists exactly the 18 delegation, genesis or direct distinctness callers; directional benchStatuses show every vs1..vs4 and decode bench pass while every s2p bench fails
OPX2-tests.tsv: all q_h*_split, fin_* and hostile rows pass; q_alias_* rows pass vacuously because distinctness is already False

callsites.mechanism: accepts1 and the cost benches conjoin s2p_on, which calls delegated, whose first conjunct is identities_distinct
genesis conjoins identities_distinct over [vi_hash, ..pieces] with the genesis policy
the test itself asserts distinctness of the honest fixture identifiers

whyNotProduction: Real compiled hashes of the distinct C2 and VS2 scripts differ; only the hand-written test stand-ins collide. Weakening identities_distinct, removing any piece, or switching back to the old VS would destroy a required binding and is prohibited. The guard, exact coverage, four withdrawals, intent, custody, digest and native checks all stay.
minimalFix: In candidate/aiken/lib/pvc2/shard4_harness.ak only, change vs2_t from 28 bytes of 0xc2 to 28 bytes of 0xd2, which collides with none of c2_hash (0xc2), vi_t (0xb1), vs1_t (0xc1), vs3_t (0xc3), vs4_t (0xc4), foreign (0xb3) or c2_hash_foreign (0xcc). Byte length and file size are unchanged, so no compiled validator size changes. Root must verify the new file digest after materialization.
